title: StackKit host maintenance result v1
description: Result of `stackkit host updates plan`, `stackkit host updates apply` and `stackkit host reboot`, carried as data of the stackkit.command-result/v1 envelope for every status. internal/hostmaintenance owns the semantics. Envelope status denied carries refusal (nothing on the host changed; exit 3); status failed carries failure (exit 1, or exit 4 with outcome running when apply stopped waiting while its update unit keeps running); status success carries neither. v1 supports Debian-family nodes with apt and systemd. Absent list fields mean empty lists. Messages are diagnostic and must not be used as policy input; codes are stable.

package_manager.description: Detected package manager; only apt is supported in v1.

plan_digest.description: sha256: plus the hex SHA-256 of the lexically sorted `name=version` lines (each terminated by LF) of the packages apply installs. Held packages are excluded. `stackkit host updates apply --plan-digest` must repeat it.

pending_count.description: Number of packages apply installs (held packages are not counted).

security_count.description: Pending packages whose candidate comes from a security archive.

packages.description: Packages apply installs, sorted by name.

held.description: Pending upgrades held by default and never installed by apply: the container runtime (docker.io, docker-engine, docker-ce*, containerd*, runc, crun, podman, moby-engine, moby-containerd, moby-runc), because upgrading it restarts every workload. The hold binds `stackkit host updates apply` only; unattended-upgrades is governed by the StackKit base policy. Apply pins every installed held package to its installed version.

hold_scope.description: Human-readable statement of the hold scope, reported with every plan.

kept_back.description: Packages apt keeps back from a plain upgrade (new dependencies or phased updates).

reboot_likely.description: The planned set updates the kernel, the C library or systemd.

dpkg_problems.description: Lines reported by `dpkg --audit`. apply refuses with dpkg_broken while any exist.

outcome.description: apply only. applied: the planned set was installed; noop: nothing was pending; failed: apt failed (changes lists what changed anyway); running: the CLI stopped waiting after 20 minutes while the update unit keeps running.

unit.description: Transient systemd unit: kombify-host-update-<digest prefix>-<unix time> for apply, kombify-host-reboot-<unix time> for reboot.

changes.description: apply only: each planned package's installed version before and after (dpkg-query). An empty version means not installed.

reboot_required.description: apply only: /var/run/reboot-required exists after the run. apply never reboots.

auto_marks_not_restored.description: apply only: planned packages that were automatically installed before and are marked manual afterwards because restoring the mark failed.

scheduled.description: reboot only: the reboot timer was created. This is the acknowledgement; the command does not wait for the reboot. When the timer fires, `stackkit host reboot-guard` checks the node again, waits up to 15 minutes for package operations and host updates, and requests the reboot while holding the host maintenance and dpkg locks; a node that stays busy, or that now runs the control plane, is not rebooted and keeps its boot ID.

boot_id_before.description: reboot only: /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id before the reboot; a different boot ID afterwards proves the node rebooted.

scheduled_at.description: reboot only: when the reboot timer fires.

refusal.description: Present with envelope status denied. Written before any side effect. package_manager_busy covers held apt/dpkg locks, a running host update, a scheduled reboot (apply) and a concurrent host maintenance operation; unattended_reboot_unsupported covers crypttab volumes whose key field is empty, none or - (unless noauto) and nodes without apt.

failure.description: Present with envelope status failed. host_probe_failed is also how reboot fails closed when it cannot rule out a Techstack control plane (for example a Docker daemon that does not answer, or a process it may not read) or read /etc/crypttab.

name.description: Package name, with :arch for a foreign architecture.
